description_full: Chemung Financial Corporation operates as a bank holding company for Chemung Canal Trust Company that provides a range of banking, financing, fiduciary, and other financial services. The company provides demand, savings, and time deposits; non-interest and interest-bearing checking accounts; and insured money market deposits. It also offers commercial and agricultural loans comprising loans to small to mid-sized businesses; commercial and residential mortgage loans; and consumer loans, including home equity lines of credit and home equity term loans, as well as automobile loans. In addition, the company provides interest rate swaps, letters of credit, employee benefit plans, insurance products, mutual fund, brokerage, and tax preparation services. Further, it offers guardian, custodian, trustee, investment, pension, estate planning, and employee benefit administrative services, as well as acts as an agent for pension, profit-sharing, and other employee benefit trusts. The company was founded in 1833 and is based in Elmira, New York.

financial_summary: Chemung Financial Corp is a small-cap financial services business with a $410M market cap on $95M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -0% over the past three years and +3% annually across the full decade — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 19% against a 7% cost of capital — a 11-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $44M in free cash flow — roughly 46 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.01× so those profits are backed by real cash.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 0.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 1.6%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 18% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
